what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat a rare inherited condition called cystinosis. In cystinosis, a substance called cystine builds up inside cells and damages organs, especially the kidneys. Cysteamine bitartrate helps break down the cystine buildup and protects your organs from damage.
how_to_take: Cystagon (immediate-release capsules): Take every 6 hours, around the clock, with food. You can swallow the capsule whole, or open it and sprinkle the contents on food like applesauce or mix into formula or juice if you have trouble swallowing. Do NOT crush or chew Procysbi capsules. Procysbi (delayed-release capsules): Take every 12 hours with food. Swallow whole, or open and sprinkle on applesauce only — do not mix into other foods or liquids. Always take with food to reduce stomach upset. Try to take your doses at the same times each day.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight (usually in kilograms). Doses are adjusted over time, often starting low and gradually increasing over 4 to 6 weeks. Your doctor will regularly check cystine levels in your white blood cells to make sure your dose is right. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Because this medicine needs to be taken regularly to work properly, try to set reminders or alarms to help you stay on schedule.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking cysteamine at the same time as antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium, as they may reduce how well the medicine works — space these apart by at least 2 hours. Avoid skipping doses, as missing doses allows cystine to build back up quickly. Tell your doctor before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it may increase stomach side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: skin rashes, sores, or blistering (especially on the elbows or knees); bone or joint pain; seizures; fever; unusual bruising or bleeding; vomiting blood or seeing blood in your stool; signs of liver problems like yellowing of the skin or eyes; severe stomach pain; confusion or changes in behavior; or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if the medicine's smell (rotten egg-like odor) becomes unbearable or if you are having trouble taking it consistently.
when_it_works: This medicine does not cure cystinosis but it helps slow down organ damage when taken consistently. You may not feel any different right away — the benefit is happening inside your cells. Your doctor will check your white blood cell cystine levels regularly (usually every 3 months) to confirm the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel well.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for use in children, including infants. Doses are carefully calculated based on weight. Parents should ask the doctor how to prepare and give the medicine if the child cannot swallow capsules. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully established. Older adults: Use in older adults should be discussed with the doctor, as dosing adjustments may be needed based on kidney function. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine.
